'''Yvette Amice''' (4 June 1936 – 4 July 1993) was a French mathematician who carried out research in the areas of [[number theory]] and [[p-adic analysis|{{mvar|p}}-adic analysis]].<ref name="bk">{{citation
 | last1 = Barsky | first1 = Daniel
 | last2 = Kahane | first2 = Jean-Pierre
 | issue = 61
 | journal = Gazette des Mathématiciens
 | mr = 1289341
 | pages = 83–87
 | title = Yvette Amice (1936–1993)
 | url = http://smf4.emath.fr/Publications/Gazette/1994/61/smf_gazette_61_82-87.pdf
 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141129013539/http://smf4.emath.fr/Publications/Gazette/1994/61/smf_gazette_61_82-87.pdf
 |archive-date=29 November 2014
| year = 1994|url-status=dead}}.</ref><ref name=im>{{cite web|url=https://cosmovisions.com/Amice.htm|title=Yvette Amice|publisher=Imago Mundi|access-date=17 June 2026}}</ref> The Amice transform and Amice theorem for ''p''-adic functions are named after her.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Shalit |first=Ehud de |date=2 January 2017 |title=Mahler bases and elementary $p$-adic analysis |url=https://jtnb.centre-mersenne.org/item/JTNB_2016__28_3_597_0/ |journal=Journal de théorie des nombres de Bordeaux |language=en |volume=28 |issue=3 |pages=597–620 |doi=10.5802/jtnb.955 |issn=2118-8572}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Chamizo |first=Fernando |url=https://www.google.fr/books/edition/Trends_in_Number_Theory/KR6jCgAAQBAJ?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=Mahler+theorem+amice&pg=PA197&printsec=frontcover |title=Trends in Number Theory |last2=Guàrdia |first2=Jordi |last3=Rojas-León |first3=Antonio |last4=Tornero |first4=José María |date=28 September 2015 |publisher=American Mathematical Soc. |isbn=978-0-8218-9858-1 |language=en}}</ref> She headed academic societies and was the second woman president of the [[Société mathématique de France]]. In addition to her academic work, she promoted recognition of women mathematicians and their achievements.<ref name="im" />

== Biography ==

=== Early life and education ===
Born on 4 June 1936, following her father's death from war injuries, she was brought up by her mother, a school teacher, in [[Indre et Loire]].<ref name="bk"/>

Amice studied mathematics at the [[École normale supérieure de jeunes filles]] in [[Sèvres]], from 1956, earning her [[agrégation]] in 1959.<ref name="bk"/> She became an assistant at the Faculté des sciences de Paris until 1964, when she completed a state doctorate under the supervision of [[André Weil]] and  [[Charles Pisot]].<ref name=im/> Her dissertation was titled ''p-adic interpolation'' ({{Langx|fr|Interpolation p-adique}}).<ref name="bk"/><ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=74639}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{citation |last=Kosmann-Schwarzbach |first=Yvette |date=2 September 2015 |title=Women mathematicians in France in the mid-twentieth century |url=https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/17498430.2014.976804 |journal=BSHM Bulletin: Journal of the British Society for the History of Mathematics |volume=30 |issue=3 |pages=227–242 |doi=10.1080/17498430.2014.976804 |issn=1749-8430|arxiv=1502.07597 }}</ref>{{Efn|The BNF includes a catalogue entry for Amice's ''Interpolation p-adique''. It was published in Paris by Gauthier-Villars in 1965. Her thesis for Sc. math. in 1964, it was first published in the Bulletin de la Société mathématique de France, T. 92, in 1964.<ref>{{citation|url=https://catalogue.bnf.fr/index.do|title=Interpolation p-adique|author=Amice, Yvette|access-date=16 May 2026}}</ref>}} Her doctoral work addressed [[p-adic L-function|''p''-adic zeta functions]] and the arithmetic of [[local field]]s.<ref name="im" /> Her procedure (now known as Amice theorem) generalized [[Mahler's theorem]].<ref>{{Cite book |last=Babbitt |first=Donald G. |url=https://www.google.fr/books/edition/Featured_Reviews_in_Mathematical_Reviews/ibwvWacJOnsC?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=mahler+bases+amice&pg=SL1-PA51&printsec=frontcover |title=Featured Reviews in Mathematical Reviews 1997–1999: With Selected Reviews of Classic Books and Papers from 1940–1969 |last2=Kister |first2=Jane E. |date=5 May 2000 |publisher=American Mathematical Soc. |isbn=978-0-8218-9670-9 |language=en}}</ref>

In 1965, she gave one of the [[Peccot Lectures]] (for distinguished mathematicians under 30 years old) at the [[Collège de France]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=LISTE CHRONOLOGIQUE DES COURS PECCOT AVEC LES INTITULÉS DEPUIS 1899 |url=https://www.college-de-france.fr/media/cours-peccot/UPL1466994975427365342_LISTE_CHRONOLOGIQUE_DES_INTITULES_DES_COURS_PECCOT_DEPUIS_1899_.pdf |website=Collège de France}}</ref>

=== Career ===
On completing her doctorate, Amice became [[maître de conférences]] (lecturer) at the [[University of Poitiers]]. In 1966, she was appointed professor at the [[University of Bordeaux]] and gave the [[Peccot Lectures|Cours Peccot]] lecture series at the [[Collège de France]].<ref name=":0" /> She was an advisor to {{Ill|Jean Fresnel|fr}} (1967) and Daniel Barksy (1974).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Yvette Amice – The Mathematics Genealogy Project |url=https://www.mathgenealogy.org/id.php?id=74639 |access-date=16 June 2026 |website=www.mathgenealogy.org}}</ref> 

Amice returned to Poitiers in 1968, then in 1970 became one of the founding professors of [[Paris Diderot University]], where she was vice president from 1978 to 1981. She was director of a seminar on number theory at the university.<ref name=":0" />

She participated in a number of significant bodies, including the CCU (1968–1976) and the CBESER (1976–1983). She headed the mathematics training and research unit (UFR) at [[Paris VII]] (1975.1978), after which she became responsible for all teaching at Paris VII (1978–1981).<ref name="bk"/>

In 1975 she became president of the [[Société mathématique de France]].<ref name="bk"/> She had been one of three vice-presidents to the society in 1974, and was the only woman on the 25-member council. She was the second woman president of the society, after [[Marie-Louise Dubreil-Jacotin]] in 1952.<ref name=":0" /> The third woman president, [[Mireille Martin-Deschamps]], did not achieve that role until 1988.<ref name=":0" /> As president of the Société mathématique, together with [[Georges Poitou]], she created the [[Centre International de Rencontres Mathématiques]] which was founded in Luminy, Marseille, in the early 1980s.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://catalogue.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/cb12392338t|title=Amice, Yvette (1936–1993)|publisher=BnF|access-date=18 June 2026}}</ref><ref name="bk"/> Together with [[Jean Giraud (mathematician)|Jean Giraud]]. she was also instrumental in creating the SCFCIEM, the French subcommission of the [[International Commission on Mathematical Instruction]].<ref name="bk"/>

Amice died from cancer in [[Passy, Haute-Savoie]], on 4 July 1993, aged 57, following a decade-long illness.<ref name=":0" /><ref name="bk"/>

== Advocacy ==
Amice was a supporter of the role of women in science at a time when academic posts were reserved principally for men. She maintained that women scientists and mathematicians should no longer be considered an exception to the general rule. As a result, she actively advocated for the support of women in a number of relevant committees and high-level academic bodies.<ref name="im" />

==Textbook==
Amice was the author of a textbook on the [[p-adic number|''p''-adic number system]], ''Les nombres p-adiques'' (Presses Universitaires de France, 1975).<ref>{{citation|url=https://search.worldcat.org/title/Les-nombres-p-adiques/oclc/2048575|title=Les nombres p-adiques|author=Amice, Yvette|publisher=Presses Universitaires de France|year=1975}}</ref> Various reviews at the time of release considered it to be a well-written introduction to [[p-adic analysis|''p''-adic analysis]] covering discussion of ''p''-adic numbers, [[non-archimedean field]]s and [[Banach space]]s, [[analytic function]]s, and [[Rational root theorem|rationality theorems]].<ref>Reviews of ''Les nombres p-adiques'':
*{{citation|jstor=2977044|journal=[[The American Mathematical Monthly]]|volume=83|issue=3|year=1976|page=216|title=Telegraphic Reviews|first=Steven|last=Galovich}}
*{{citation|mr=0447195|first=W.|last=Bartenwerfer|journal=[[Mathematical Reviews]]|title=none}}
*{{citation|first=A.|last=Escassut|journal=[[zbMATH]]|title=none|zbl=0313.12104}}</ref>

==Honours and awards==
In 1963, Amice was awarded the Albert Châtelet Medal for her works in ''p''-adic analysis.<ref>{{Cite journal |date=1964 |title=Médaille Albert Châtelet |journal=L'Enseignement mathématique |language=fr |volume=10 |page=176|url=https://www.e-periodica.ch/digbib/view?pid=ens-001%3A1964%3A10%3A%3A262}}</ref>

She was decorated as a knight of the [[Legion of Honour]] in January 1991.<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.lemonde.fr/archives/article/1991/01/03/legion-d-honneur_4017485_1819218.html|title=Legion d'Honneur|publisher=Le Monde|date=3 January 1991|access-date=14 May 2026}} </ref>

In 2026, Amice was announced as one of 72 historical women in STEM whose names have been proposed to be added to the [[List of the 72 names on the Eiffel Tower|72 men]] already celebrated on the [[Eiffel Tower]]. The plan was conceived by a student and tour guide named Bernard Rigaud and it was taken up by Sorbonne University's President [[Nathalie Drach-Temam]].<ref name="rigaud">{{Cite web |title=The Hypatia project: engraving the names of 72 women scientists on the Eiffel Tower |url=https://www.sorbonne-universite.fr/en/news/hypatia-project-engraving-names-72-women-scientists-eiffel-tower |access-date=15 June 2026 |website=Sorbonne Université |language=en}}</ref> and it was announced by the Mayor of Paris, [[Anne Hidalgo]] following the recommendations of a committee led by [[Isabelle Vauglin]] of [[Femmes et Sciences]] and Jean-François Martins, representing the operating company which runs the Eiffel Tower.<ref>{{citation |title=Eiffel Tower: a list of 72 women scientists will soon be inscribed on the Parisian monument |url=https://www.sortiraparis.com/en/news/in-paris/articles/340564-eiffel-tower-list-of-72-women-scientists-soon-to-be-honored-on-the-paris-landmark |access-date=2 February 2026 |website=www.sortiraparis.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{citation |title=Les noms des 72 femmes pour la Tour Eiffel ont été révélés. |url=https://www.femmesetsciences.fr/news/les-noms-des-72-femmes-pour-la-tour-eiffel-ont-%C3%A9t%C3%A9-r%C3%A9v%C3%A9l%C3%A9 |access-date=22 February 2026 |website=Femmes & Sciences |language=fr}}</ref><ref>[https://10ca8303-b3dc-4a91-9dcc-2d2b91792b47.usrfiles.com/ugd/10ca83_3838bd19a41a4e83927cfc8fe0f50404.pdf 72 femmes de sciences pour la tour Eiffel] ''Femmes & Sciences'' (in French). Retrieved 22 February 2026</ref><ref name=":1">{{citation |date=26 January 2026 |title=Eiffel Tower to honor 72 women scientists for posterity |url=https://www.lemonde.fr/en/france/article/2026/01/26/eiffel-tower-to-honor-72-women-in-science-for-posterity_6749828_7.html |access-date=3 February 2026 |language=en}}</ref>
